usda-mass-firings-inspection-collapse-20.why: A judge ruled the Office of Personnel Management's directive behind the probationary firings, including at USDA, was unlawful, but declined to order reinstatement.

usda-snap-data-demand-reapplication-frau.why: A judge's preliminary injunction found 21 states and D.C. likely to succeed on claims that USDA's SNAP data demand and threatened funding cutoff were contrary to law under the APA.

usda-tribal-farm-grants-terminated-2026.why: A judge's preliminary injunction found USDA's terminations of 24 of the program's grants were likely contrary to statute; the D.C. Circuit denied USDA a stay.

usip-doge-takeover-trump2.why: A judge ruled the President's removal of USIP's board unlawful and voided the takeover; an appeals court largely stayed that ruling, finding USIP "exercises substantial executive power."

va-abortion-services-ban-2025-2026.who: VA Secretary Doug Collins and the Department of Veterans Affairs
va-abortion-services-ban-2025-2026.why: A pending Federal Circuit petition by Minority Veterans of America alleges the VA's abortion-ban rule is arbitrary and capricious, a possible Administrative Procedure Act violation.

va-mass-firings-early-2025.why: A judge ruled OPM lacked authority to direct the probationary firings, including at the VA, and ordered records corrected but no rehiring; the government's appeal is pending.

va-warrior-independence-center-unfunded-.why: A judge's housing order, largely upheld on appeal, rests on a finding that VA violated the Rehabilitation Act; the order is paused while VA weighs a Supreme Court petition.

vasquez-perdomo-noem-la-racial-profiling.why: A judge held the government in civil contempt in July 2026, finding by clear and convincing evidence it failed to image agents' phones as ordered; it still pays the daily fine.
An October 2026 preliminary injunction found plaintiffs likely to show a policy of stops based on racial stereotyping that violates the Fourth Amendment; it is paused on appeal.
The same October 2026 injunction found the race-based stops policy likely violates the Fifth Amendment's equal protection guarantee; the Ninth Circuit paused it pending appeal.
A November 2025 preliminary injunction found plaintiffs likely to succeed on a Fifth Amendment access-to-counsel claim over lawyer access at the B-18 holding area.

voa-usagm-dismantlement-trump2.who: Kari Lake, Senior Adviser to the President and former acting CEO of USAGM
voa-usagm-dismantlement-trump2.why: A judge ruled Kari Lake unlawfully ran USAGM, citing the Federal Vacancies Reform Act, and voided her actions there, including the August 2025 layoffs.

voa-usagm-dismantlement-trump2.who: Kari Lake, Senior Adviser to the President and former acting CEO of USAGM
voa-usagm-dismantlement-trump2.why: The same ruling cited the Constitution's Appointments Clause in finding an unlawful effort to make Lake USAGM's CEO "in all but name" and voiding her actions.
A judge vacated USAGM's memorandum cutting VOA to a statutory minimum as arbitrary and capricious; an appeals court paused his order returning staff to work.

vought-impoundment-control-act-2025-2026.who: Russell Vought, Director of the Office of Management and Budget
vought-impoundment-control-act-2025-2026.why: GAO found the administration's withholding of funds Congress approved violated the Impoundment Control Act in seven decisions; Vought, who directed it at OMB, calls the law unconstitutional.

wiles-ap-press-access-2025.who: Susie Wiles, White House Chief of Staff at the time
wiles-ap-press-access-2025.why: A judge granted AP a preliminary injunction, finding it was excluded over its Stylebook's viewpoint; an appeals panel stayed it except for the East Room while the appeal is pending.

wright-faca-violation-2026.who: Chris Wright, Secretary of Energy, and the U.S. Department of Energy
wright-faca-violation-2026.why: A federal judge ruled that DOE's Climate Working Group was a federal advisory committee whose FACA violations were "established as matter of law."
A pending lawsuit alleges DOE appointees used personal email to conduct the climate working group's business, which may violate the Federal Records Act.

zeldin-dissent-letter-retaliation-2025-2.who: Lee Zeldin, Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency
zeldin-dissent-letter-retaliation-2025-2.why: Fired probationary EPA staff sued, alleging their firings for signing a personal-capacity dissent letter violated the First Amendment; an EPA lawyer called the letter likely protected speech.
